#3240. Report: Apple faces congressional scrutiny over ICE tracking apps and Trump donations

Reuters and The Washington Post report that Apple is among the tech giants potentially facing congressional investigations as Democrats prepare to take control of both chambers in January. Here are the details.

Earlier today, The Washington Post reported that “Democrats are laying the groundwork to investigate some of the country’s largest companies, setting off a scramble among executives who courted the president.”

The report notes that Washington law firms are advising companies and executives on how to prepare for potential congressional investigations, with some also pitching their services to Elon Musk:

Multiple firms have crafted pitches for why they should serve as Musk’s personal counsel, aware that the world’s richest man is likely to receive a barrage of subpoenas and that any casework stemming from those investigations will be both lucrative and the highest-profile investigative work available in the coming year, according to two of the people.

When it comes to Apple, the report noted that lawmakers are gearing up to investigate the company “over its hosting of tracking apps used by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.”

While the report refers to Apple’s hosting of tracking apps used by ICE, the company has previously faced scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers over its decision to remove apps used to track ICE agents from the App Store.

Last year, Apple removed ICEBlock and several similar apps from the App Store following pressure from the DOJ, citing concerns over the safety of federal agents.

The move came shortly after a gunman opened fire on an ICE facility in Dallas, ultimately killing two detainees in an attack that federal authorities described as targeted violence against ICE.

Since then, Apple has faced questions from Democratic lawmakers over the extent of the Trump administration’s involvement in the decision and whether the removals infringed on constitutionally protected speech.

“over its hosting of tracking apps used by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.”

The word “by” seems important here. That quote is clearly not about the apps used to track ICE, it’s about apps that ICE uses itself.

That makes me wonder if the original article is confused, though. Is ICE really “hosting” its own internal apps on the App Store rather than deploying through some enterprise/MDM distribution method? I guess Apple is involved in that process, too? And if the incoming Congress takes the posture that ICE has been operating an illegal human trafficking ring, then assisting them is a crime.

Apple was pathetic and ridiculous for removing ICEBlock and similar apps. It was also blatantly unconstitutional for the DOJ to threaten them into doing it.

Reuters, meanwhile, reported that Senator Richard Blumenthal, “who is set to take over as chair of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations,” called on Apple “and others who donated to [President Trump’s new White House] ballroom project to turn over records” or “face possible subpoenas in January.”

As The Washington Post reported last month, Apple and Nvidia each pledged $25 million toward the ballroom, making them two of the project’s largest donors.

Apple did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters or The Washington Post.

You can read the full Reuters report here, and The Washington Post’s here.

#3239. Researchers asked people to use AI chatbots for election info – results were mixed

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Chatbots can skew election-related information and act as an intervening layer in a voter's search.

Most search tools now put a layer of AI between you and the information you’re looking for, especially Google.

Also: Tired of AI Overviews? I found 9 Google Search alternatives

In a new study, Yale researchers found that a third of users asked a chatbot to help them pick a candidate. Grok often recommended candidates on its own without any information from users, while ChatGPT recommended candidates most often overall, and twice as much as Claude.

The researchers asked nearly 2,500 people in 35 states with Senate races to query ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or Gemini about the election. Participants in the study, which ran for a few weeks in October leading up to the Nov. 3 midterm elections, were adults who already use chatbots weekly.

Most users asked chatbots for basic facts about the election, including who was on the ballot. But 36% asked a chatbot to help them pick a candidate to vote for, often by describing their priorities and asking the chatbot to assess which candidates aligned with them.

The former query has slightly less room for error, because the internet has a ton of data on the basic facts of an election, such as who is running where. Chatbots interpreting candidate positions, on the other hand, is a bit more dicey, and relies significantly on the sources a chatbot uses (a statement from a candidate’s own website, for example, is more reliable than a social media clip of an opponent characterizing them in a certain way).

Also: How to keep your chatbot conversations as private as possible

In one example, a user asked ChatGPT to give them the “pros and cons” of each candidate in Virginia, an inherently subjective question.

When it came to recommending candidates, chatbots varied widely.

“When users asked who to vote for but had not yet said anything about themselves, only Grok regularly recommended a candidate, in 14% of chats,” the researchers wrote. “Once users shared their views, ChatGPT recommended a candidate in 79% of chats and Claude in 40%, with Grok and Gemini in between.”

Pew Research found that 42% of US adults surveyed use chatbots to search for information. That’s a broad umbrella that can include election information — but Pew also found that only 8% of US adults reported using chatbots to find election-related information in this year’s election.

What those users are looking for matters, though. Pew found that of that group, 76% were inquiring about where candidates stand on certain issues, and 71% were fact-checking information they’d heard about candidates or issues.

Also: OpenAI will merge ChatGPT’s chat and work tabs

Given that chatbots are still not reliable summarizers, the nature of these questions poses a misinformation risk if users don’t also check a chatbot’s linked sources. An overwhelming majority of users don’t, at least when it comes to Google’s AI Overviews. At least one study found AI platforms gave users “outdated or inaccurate” information that could mislead voters in some cases by missing a deadline or failing to mention a step about voting logistics.

This election cycle was particularly plagued by AI-generated deepfakes and misinformation as tools have become much more sophisticated since the 2024 election. OpenAI and Anthropic reportedly set up election “war rooms” to monitor misuse and information accuracy, according to exclusive reporting by Politico and Semafor.

While an August study from the Brennan Center for Justice found that chatbots did push back surprisingly well against certain falsehoods related to election disinformation campaigns, it also found that AI models easily generated “misleading election-related images and video” when asked.

“Many of their safeguards for preventing this were ineffective, inconsistently applied, or functionally absent,” noted the study, which tested ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Meta AI, Runway, and Flux.2.

Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well

Apart from these factors, however, there is a broader theme in AI use that is equally consequential for civic engagement: cognitive offloading. The political media landscape can already be dense and hard to parse for a voter trying to stay informed. Layering a chatbot — which has opaque training data sets, filters, and other settings determined at the discretion of AI labs — on top of that information search process can further muddy the waters while appearing like a convenient and neutral summarizing tool.

While some studies test how AI chatbots respond to election questions by using standardized questions, this approach let users themselves engage with chatbots as they normally would. While the Yale researchers’ queries and standardized study queries show a lot of similarities, the distinction is valuable for evaluations.

“This is a small step toward evaluations that measure AI’s political influence on the questions users actually ask,” the researchers noted.

Outside of users self-reporting what they asked a chatbot, only AI labs have records of what users are really asking about elections. In October, Anthropic analyzed 250,000 conversations with Claude and determined people “rarely ask Claude whom or what to vote for,” finding that “0.51% of all conversations are specifically about elections or voting,” though it expected election-related queries to increase closer to Nov. 3.

Also: 6 AI agent workflows I use to hand off everyday tasks

“More often, we observed people asking Claude questions that could help them reach their own conclusions, like where candidates stand on a particular issue. Requests that violated our election integrity policies were even less common, appearing in about 0.002% of conversations,” Anthropic’s report said.

The Yale researchers said the next step for a study like theirs is determining how accurate and unbiased models are in their responses, as well as what models learn about users, and whether their recommendations actually match users’ needs.

“In multi-turn chats, users often answered the chatbot’s questions, and those answers led to its recommendations. The questions a model asks shape what users tell it and what it recommends,” the researchers explained.

#3237. Hims & Hers Health vs. Intuitive Surgical: Which Healthcare Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Both are disruptors, but one of these growth stocks stands out over the other.

Investors seeking long-term growth often weigh the disruptive potential of telehealth against the proven dominance of medical robotics. Choosing between Hims & Hers Health (HIMS +8.06%) and Intuitive Surgical (ISRG -3.35%) depends on your appetite for risk and valuation.

Both companies operate within the healthcare sector but serve different ends of the market. Hims & Hers Health focuses on direct-to-consumer digital wellness and personalized prescriptions. Intuitive Surgical builds the complex hardware and software systems that surgeons use to perform minimally invasive procedures in hospitals around the world.

Hims & Hers Health operates a digital platform that connects patients with licensed healthcare providers. The company sells personalized treatment plans for hair loss, sexual health, mental health, and weight loss. Its business model relies on a substantial majority of revenue from recurring subscription purchases of prescription medications. By utilizing partner pharmacies for fulfillment and affiliated medical groups for consultations, the company maintains a scalable infrastructure.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $2.3 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 59% compared to the previous year. This rapid expansion followed a strong FY 2024, where revenue reached close to $1.5 billion. The company reported net income of roughly $128.4 million for the 2025 fiscal period. This performance marks a significant shift toward profitability after reporting a net loss in earlier years.

Intuitive Surgical is a leader among medical device stocks due to its da Vinci surgical system. This platform allows for robotic-assisted surgery, which often leads to shorter recovery times for patients. The company generates revenue through system sales, recurring service contracts, and the sale of disposable instruments. Its primary customers are large hospitals and health systems that integrate these platforms into their operating rooms.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $10 billion, which is a 20.5% increase over the prior year. The company reported a net income of approximately $2.9 billion, resulting in a net margin of roughly 28.4%. This high net margin reflects the percentage of revenue that remains as profit after all expenses are paid. The steady growth in procedure volumes continues to drive the demand for new systems and ongoing instrument replacement.

Hims & Hers Health faces significant regulatory and legal scrutiny, particularly regarding its compounded weight-loss products. Investigations by the DOJ and potential FDA restrictions could disrupt its core operations. The company also depends heavily on third-party medical groups and pharmacies for fulfillment. Furthermore, it is currently involved in patent infringement litigation with Novo Nordisk and competes against well-funded incumbents in a market where brand differentiation is difficult to maintain.

Intuitive Surgical faces competition from major players such as Medtronic (MDT -2.90%) and Johnson & Johnson. These rivals are developing their own robotic surgical platforms, which could lead to pricing pressure. The company is also managing ongoing product liability and antitrust litigation, including a recent $450 million settlement charge. Because its revenue model depends on procedure volumes, any global disruption to elective surgeries or hospital budget cuts poses a risk to its financial results.

While Hims & Hers Health appears more affordable based on its sales multiple, Intuitive Surgical trades at a significantly lower multiple of its future earnings estimates.

With both of these companies in the medical field, they carry noticeable risk, so it is best to treat each as a more speculative position. For instance, neither company is performing particularly well in 2026, with the share price of Intuitive down 17.2%, while the share price of Hims & Hers is down nearly 26%. But if there could only be one winner between the two, I would lean toward picking Intuitive. The main reason is the uniqueness of its product offerings and the moat that it has created. Being a trusted equipment provider in robot-assisted surgery, even if there is some growing competition, helps create a moat, as not just anyone can build a similar company and instantly receive orders from hospitals. And being that trusted provider helps lead to more repeat customers. For instance, in the third quarter of 2026, Intuitive grew its da Vinci surgical system installed base to 12,094 systems, an increase of 12% compared to the prior-year period. Intuitive also reported revenue of $3 billion for the quarter, an increase of 22%.

In comparison, Hims & Hers has a narrower moat, serving more as a platform that connects consumers with products. It's also becoming an increasingly competitive space, with pharmaceutical companies launching their own direct-to-consumer and direct-to-patient platforms, such as Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk. To reemphasize, both of these companies have their challenges and should be considered more speculative positions. But Intuitive stands out for its better moat.

#3234. iOS 27.3: New features, release date, more

This week, Apple released the first iOS 27.3 beta. The update includes multiple new features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 …

As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final update.

The redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 users, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

For Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo users, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left to make it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with new clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The update also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the update expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test new ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to new languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:

iOS 27.3 is a major update to Safari. First, the update adds support for a new vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

For Apple Music users, iOS 27.3 adds a new “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The update also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

I tested Modern Sprout's handsome Growframe for a pop of green during fall and winter.

My pursuit of good houseplant tools means I’m always looking for shops and resources. That led me to Modern Sprout, a Chicago-based online store that sells plants and plant-care accessories. When they reached out offering a chance to test some of its high-design indoor garden tech, I decided to see what, if anything, is worth considering for your houseplant needs or as a place to get gifts for the plant parents in your life. I found a few pleasant surprises.

Whether I’m tending to houseplants in winter or gardening in summer, I’m always looking for tools to improve plant care. For houseplants in particular, this means watering, trimming, fertilizing, occasionally repotting and providing as much real estate in sunny windows as possible. When that’s not enough, I harness the power of full-spectrum LED grow lights, so I can have greenery in practically every room of my apartment.

A quick look at Modern Sprout’s website shows it sells most of what you’d expect from a boutique plant nursery: live plants, potting soil, gardening accessories, grow lights, grow kits, candles, bird feeders and gift sets. While Modern Sprout carries plenty of its own products, it also curates items from other small businesses instead of relying on large mainstream gardening brands. This is a nice bonus for folks who prefer to support smart business owners. Modern Sprout also offers wholesale accounts, so you might even see it at a nursery near you.

For my tests, I stuck to the Modern Sprout brand, which is also available on Amazon. Since I review a lot of smart home gear, I wanted to try out the Smart Landscape Growframe ($229) and compare it with other plant light options I use. I also wanted to see if Modern Sprout’s tools are any good, so I rounded out my experience with three essentials behind effective houseplant care: Pruning Shears ($20), a Glass Watering Can ($48) and Dissolving Plant Food Sheets ($20).

I don’t think anything could’ve prepared me for the size of the Smart Landscape Growframe: 32.1 inches long, 11.5 inches tall and 5.3 inches deep. For some context, that’s wider than my kitchen table and large enough to require a careful survey of my home to find a suitable location. I found a nice spot above my stairs next to the front door.

Additionally, its durable powder-coated steel frame weighs an incredible 8 pounds. That’s roughly the weight of a gallon of milk, which makes wall mounting tricky. I agree with Modern Sprout’s recommendation to place the mounting screws in studs, so you’ll need a stud finder, a level, and a power drill if you want it on the wall. You can use drywall anchors, but they aren’t included.

Make sure you visually line up the Growframe’s mounting holes with your marks before driving screws into the wall. This is easier with a second person, but I managed it alone. However, I relied purely on my measurements and had to redo the screws after one was slightly off. I suggest marking one stud first, then holding the planter and using a level to see where the other should go. Similarly, keep in mind that the 9-foot power cord needs to reach an outlet.

The app isn’t complex and is really easy to use. I really like that there are preset schedules for shade, partial sun and full sun light levels — these options always start at 8 a.m., providing 8, 12 and 16 hours of lighting at different intensities, respectively. The presets aren’t customizable, so you must use one of the app’s two other scheduling options to adjust the timing and other settings. I noticed that toggling a preset works as intended, but closing and reopening the menu shows an inactive toggle — a minor visual bug that doesn’t seem to affect the feature. (It might even get patched by the time you read this review.)

You can also set a schedule using specific times of day in the Growframe device menu. While this particular scheduling menu lacks an option to tie the lighting controls to sunrise and sunset, you can find that on the Scenario tab. (Sunrise/sunset automation isn’t necessary for most tropical plants and herbs people put in the planter, but it’s nice to have a temperate lighting option that changes throughout the year.)

The Scenario tab offers a few automation options based on device status, scheduling and weather changes, plus a way to set up manual Tap-to-Run automations. Beyond that, there isn’t much else to the app, which makes sense and aligns with the company’s goal of keeping things simple. However, folks wanting smart home integrations with a platform like Home Assistant or Samsung SmartThings might be better off using a smart plug with a different grow light brand.

Speaking of grow lights, the full-spectrum unit inside the top of the Smart Landscape Growframe can reach up to 1,480 lumens, which is very bright considering most plants in the planter will be within 6 inches or less. Given the size limit on the plants you can put in the planter, I doubt you’ll have any issues with giving your plants enough light. I want to note that the adhesive holding one of the grow light strips in my sample unit came loose during shipping, but it was easy enough to reattach.

Planting in the Smart Landscape Growframe is fairly easy. It comfortably holds up to seven potted plants (2- to 3-inch pots), though I ended up putting five 4-inch potted herbs in my setup. One pot in particular is a little taller than the planter box lip, but it doesn’t bother me.

Be mindful of pot size in the planter, as rims that press up against the side can cause water to overflow onto the floor, as it did with mine. The best solution is to remove a little soil from overfilled pots and to add a small notch or hole in a side of the pot that drains into the basin.

The potted herbs I got from my local garden center needed a little trimming before I could put them in the Smart Landscape Growframe, so it was a good opportunity to try out the Pruning Shears. I’m a huge fan of the all-metal design, which is easily one of the most comfortable pairs of gardening shears I’ve used. The nifty locking latch at the end of the handle isn’t metal — it doesn’t need to be — but it’s easy to use and doesn’t require any fiddling.

I also love the needle-nose blades, which are easy to maneuver into tight spaces when trimming dead growth off plants — they are great for trimming all of my herbs. Although I’ll admit that the densely packed chives tested my patience, that’s hardly the shears’ fault.

Of the items I tested, the glass watering can was my least favorite. For instance, the borosilicate glass may be more durable than other types of glass, but it’s still glass and still fragile. I’m not sure if I trust my clumsy self with it when I water my plants. Similarly, the 1-quart size is great for folks caring for a handful of plants, but it can’t keep up with the gallon-size watering can that I sometimes empty completely just to water my dwarf lemon tree in a large container.

Another issue I had with the glass watering can was the upper rim. While I like that the flared rim makes it easy to fill from my bathroom sink, it can get in the way when watering the Growframe. This is especially tedious when you need to tilt the watering can nearly vertical to get the last drops out. Fortunately, you can see when the water is almost gone, but that’s the only real advantage it has over my normal watering can.

I often put off fertilizing houseplants because it feels like a hassle. My main reason is that most of the carnivorous plants I grow don’t like fertilizer, so I skip it on other houseplants. (I get around this with plant food spikes, but I’m hardly consistent at that either.) A secondary reason is that keeping the fertilizer out where I’ll use it isn’t the best use of space in my apartment. While Modern Sprout’s Dissolving Plant Food Sheets don’t really solve the former problem, they’re very convenient for the latter.

Just like when I tested dishwasher detergent sheets, I really like how easy it is to toss Modern Sprout’s fertilizer into the watering can. A full sheet treats a gallon and has perforations so you can tear it into segments to fit your watering can. Since the glass watering can holds one quart, I needed only one-quarter of a sheet. The sheets dissolved a little slowly, and I had to stir them for a minute or two before no fragments were left.

I’m a fan of the seaweed sheets, which are a great option for plant food that isn’t entirely a collection of processed chemicals. Despite the seaweed ingredient, the sheets don’t explicitly state they’re certified organic, so keep that in mind if you use them for herbs or microgreens.

All of the Modern Sprout products I tested have a premium design and build quality that makes them easy to recommend for people who value form as much as function. I consider the Pruning Shears the best value in the bunch. They feel incredibly sturdy and capable for $20 and are a huge step up from my $10 Vivosun Gardening Scissors in every way. I haven’t tested Modern Sprout Bypass Hand Pruners, but I suspect they’ll easily rival the Fiskars Shears I use for thicker growth.

While $229 is a lot to ask for the Smart Landscape Growframe, keep in mind that premium heavy-duty steel planters without smart lighting already cost more than those made from other materials. Likewise, more affordable — and more powerful — grow lights are on the market, but Modern Sprout’s intuitive app includes every scheduling and customization feature I consider essential. Even people who don’t use other smart home gear should find it easy to navigate.

I think the Dissolving Plant Food Sheets are a fairly nice option for seaweed-based fertilizers, but the 20-pack will treat only 20 gallons of water at the normal dilution. This makes the sheets generally more expensive per feeding than liquid kelp fertilizers from brands like TPS Nutrients and Grow Queen. That said, Modern Sprout is more convenient to measure, and it won’t cause a liquid or powdery mess if you knock the package over. It’s a great gift, but not necessarily for an enthusiast with a large collection of houseplants.

I wouldn’t buy the Glass Watering Can, but I don’t think it’s a bad product. It’s undeniably attractive, but $48 is more than most. I’ll stick with my cheaper, larger plastic watering can. Overall, Modern Sprout suits folks with higher budgets or as an attractive gift option for your favorite plant nerd.

#3232. Sweetgreen Is Finally Growing Again. Time To Buy?

Sweetgreen posted same-store sales growth in October. Is it the beginning of a turnaround?

After nearly two years of declining same-store sales, Sweetgreen (SG +3.98%) has returned to growth.

While the company's third-quarter performance was marred by the Cyclospora outbreak, management said that October results were positive, with same-store sales up 5% and traffic up 4%. The company also raised its full-year guidance, showing that it may have finally emerged from a long retreat over the last two years.

Is this a buy signal for the fast-casual stock? Let's take a look at the third-quarter results and discuss the company's prospects moving forward.

Sweetgreen's third quarter was reminiscent of the brand's recent struggles, though most of the numbers can be pinned on the Cyclospora outbreak, which did not directly affect Sweetgreen but dissuaded consumers from visiting salad chains. Sweetgreen was implicated by association.

Same-store sales in the quarter fell 6.4%, and revenue ticked up 2.1% to $176 million, which beat estimates at $169.4 million. Restaurant-level profit margin fell from 13.1% to 10.4%, and its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) loss expanded from $4.4 million to $6.8 million.

On a generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) basis, its per-share loss narrowed from $0.31 to $0.26, which was slightly better than expectations of a loss of $0.27 per share. CEO Jonathan Neman redirected investor focus to the future, saying, "We believe our Sweet Growth Transformation Plan is beginning to take hold, with sales improving through the quarter and positive comparable sales in October, primarily driven by transaction growth."

Sweetgreen raised its guidance for the full year, calling for same-store sales to be down 5.5%, better than a previous range of -7% to-8%, implying 3.4% growth in the fourth quarter. It sees 10 net new restaurant openings and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $20 million-$23 million, compared to an earlier range of a $23 million-$27 million loss.

Now that Sweetgreen has returned to same-store sales growth, the next goal is to return to margin growth, assuming it can maintain the comparable sales growth.

The company is still significantly underwater from its peak in 2024. Its average unit volume (sales per restaurant) clocked in at $2.47 million in the third quarter, down from $2.92 million at the end of 2024. To get back there, Sweetgreen will have to grow same-store sales by nearly 20%, which could take several years, and open new stores with solid AUVs. Sweetgreen reported a restaurant-level profit margin of 17% in 2024 and expected it to rise to 20% in 2025, before it ran into a raft of challenges, causing the stock to plummet.

Following the successful launch of its wraps this spring, Sweetgreen is relaunching its plates menu, which includes dishes like rotisserie chicken and caramelized garlic steak, as part of a strategy to grow its dinner business and diversify further away from salads. Management also said it expected restaurant-level profit margins to benefit from more efficient labor and supply chain spending.

Sweetgreen stock rose 4% on Friday as investors applauded the improved guidance and return to growth. The stock currently trades at a price-to-sales ratio of 2, meaning if it achieved a 10% profit margin, it would have a price-to-earnings ratio of 20.

Sweetgreen is a long way from achieving such a profit margin, but the company still has a lot of growth potential. While the company has slowed its new store openings to work on operations, it still sees room in the market for at least 1,000 locations, more than triple the 290 it currently has.

If it can move toward that goal while growing same-store sales and improving profitability, the stock should be a long-term winner.

Jeremy Bowman has positions in Sweetgreen. The Motley Fool recommends Sweetgreen. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.

#3231. Linux Mint 27 arrives next month, and I like it already: New features and other upgrades to expect

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Linux

It starts with a surprise version number: Linux Mint 27 instead of 24. But the next release brings far more changes than that.

Linux Mint, my favorite Linux desktop distribution, is ready for a fresh start.

Its lead developer, Clement “Clem” Lefebvre, announced earlier this year that the team behind it was considering slowing Mint’s release cadence because the old twice-a-year release cycle was time-consuming and constrained their ability to make major changes. So it is that the next release, Linux Mint 27, will appear in your Christmas stocking.

Also: 5 premium Linux distros absolutely worth paying for in 2026

The developers officially changed the designation on Oct. 13th when Mint changed both its release cadence and its numbering. Clem’s happy about the change: it “was a tough decision to make, but we’re really starting to see it pay off. We’re taking on projects and implementing changes which would previously have been considered too large or ambitious.”

The new Mint will use Ubuntu 26.04 Long Term Support (LTS) as its base. As before, it will offer Cinnamon, Xfce, and MATE desktops.

Earlier development snapshots had been labeled Mint 23 “Alfa.” That title was explicitly a placeholder while the team decided its release strategy. Its final name is Adrien. Moving ahead, release numbers will be based on the upcoming year. Clem said, “We’ll no longer use point releases, so the release after that will be 28. You’ll upgrade from 27 to 28 to 29, and so on.” Instead of girls’ names, Mint will use boys’ names for distro titles.

On Halloween, Clem announced the top changes in Mint 27. It starts with Mint bringing hibernation back into its supported desktop configuration through a dedicated Sleep Modes page in its System Administration tool. The page is intended to make enabling and configuring hibernation easier, including addressing its swap-space requirements.

It may not sound like much, but Clem explained it’s actually rather a big deal. “When you close the lid of your laptop, it goes into a sleep mode called “Suspend”. This mode is very useful… but it has a major limitation: It uses power.” People often forget it’s not really off and that your laptop will eventually run out of power. When that happens, “the outcome is worse than a normal shutdown. The session is gone, and the battery is empty.”

Also: Linux Mint vs. RefreshOS: I compared the two best distros for new users

That’s where “Hibernation comes into play. It saves the session to disk and completely shuts down the computer. No power is used. When you reopen the lid, the session is as it was, and so is the battery.”

Another new feature is Superlight. This fresh system-monitoring application replaces the older GNOME System Monitor. It comes with CPU, RAM, swap, GPU, network, disk I/O, temperature, and fan-speed graphs. It also includes per-application and per-process resource views. Battery-equipped systems also get charge and power-flow history.

Its storage analysis is particularly interesting: it can break down disk usage into files and folders, Steam games, and Flatpak applications. That brings several common troubleshooting tasks — “What’s using the CPU?” and “Where did my disk space go?” — into one interface. I’ve been checking it out on a Mint virtual machine (VM), and I like it already.

The Nemo file manager is getting a media preview pane, toggled with F7 or a status-bar button. It supports pictures, audio, and video, and displays associated information — for photographs, that can include the capture date and camera model. I like this feature a lot. I’ve always done a lot of work from file managers going all the way back to the classic Norton Commander and its Linux successor, Midnight Commander.

I’ve said it before, I’ll say it again. You don’t need to ever touch a Linux shell via a terminal to use Mint. But if, like me, you’re an old-school Linux user and you like using the terminal, Velocitty, Mint’s new terminal application, looks interesting. Its announced features include:

The point is to make recurring projects and SSH sessions easier to find and reopen. If you like other terminal programs, my latest fave is the Rust-based WexTerm; you don’t have to use Velocitty.

Unfold is a new archive manager for viewing, creating, and extracting archives. It uses 7-Zip and 7zip-RAR and supports the encryption formats those backends handle, including password-protected archives. Its design goal is simplicity rather than a sprawling feature set.

The new Mint uses Ubuntu 26.04 LTS as its foundation. Mint is also moving from Ubiquity to the Linux Mint Debian Edition live installer for installing the operating system. This fresh installer comes with support for OEM bulk-produced installations, installation on both BIOS and EFI PCs, support for Secure Boot, and LVM/LUKS configurations.

Also: Linux Mint vs. Zorin OS: I’ve tried both Windows alternatives, and here’s my winner

For the Linux kernel, Mint 27 will use version 7.0. Which one exactly? Good question. We’ll see closer to Christmas.

Wayland compatibility remains the goal, but X11 isn’t disappearing. As Clem said in June, “In an ideal scenario, we manage to make Wayland work just as well as X11.” But they’re not there yet.

The central change is a cleanup of existing code. Mint’s longer cycle gives developers room to overhaul several parts of the desktop together, rather than squeezing individual improvements into six-month windows. As Clem put it in the September newsletter, “I don’t think I’ve ever seen so many changes and new features implemented for a single release.”

What that means for you and me will be better laptop power management, more capable built-in utilities, and a more complete collection of everyday desktop applications. For example, I expect the updated Mint will ship with GIMP 3.2.2 as its default photo editor, instead of Mint 22.3’s years-old GIMP 2.10.

Backlog doubled this year as international demand reshaped the growth outlook.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Lyntris Inc. (LYNX +28.66%) reported third quarter results characterized by significant revenue growth and a more than twofold increase in total backlog since the start of the fiscal year. Management reported that expansion is occurring across all mission domains, particularly within the Air & Missile Defense and Space ISR & Resilient Communications segments, which both saw triple-digit revenue growth. The company stated that its merchant supplier model allows it to support multiple prime contractors while maintaining high ownership of design intellectual property, which accounts for 85% of product revenue. Following its August IPO, the company has reduced its net leverage ratio to 1.2x and established a new $300 million credit facility to support future working capital needs and strategic initiatives.

Brian Morrison: Thank you, Nathan, and welcome, everyone. I'm excited to share Lyntris' third quarter results. I'll then return for our outlook and priorities before we take your questions. In August, Lyntris made its debut on the New York Stock Exchange. That IPO strengthened our balance sheet and increased our capacity to invest in the business and support future growth.

Our focus now is to build on the strong business momentum we experienced leading up to the IPO and which we have continued to see since the listing. We'll continue to execute as these programs advance, translating today's opportunities into sustained long-term growth. Our purpose is straightforward. These results exceeded our expectations, demonstrating strong momentum in our business as we continue executing against our strategic priorities. Our third quarter performance reflects strong customer demand and the increasing relevance of our technology to evolving mission requirements.

Customers need to detect threats at greater distances, operate across more frequency bands, and respond with greater speed and accuracy. Those requirements closely suit the capabilities we brought together at Lyntris, from sensing and communications to software that connects information to command and control. We see broad-based growth across a number of programs, particularly in Air & Missile Defense and Space ISR & Resilient Comms, supported by the modernization of U.S. and allied radar systems and the growing need for resilient space-based communications. International customers are also investing in sovereign defense and space capabilities, creating additional opportunities for our technology.

Much of this increased activity supports well-funded high-priority programs with room to grow as programs move through the development life cycle. This work includes upfront engineering and initial production that generate revenue and adjusted EBITDA today but also establish the technology and manufacturing foundation for follow-on work. The first system requires more engineering effort, subsequent systems build on that work, creating the opportunity for higher margins as production expands. These program positions are an essential part of our long-term growth strategy. Engaging with customers early on allows us to embed our technology in their solutions and expand our role as programs mature. That customer demand is also reflected in our backlog. Our book-to-bill in the quarter was 1.5. Even with the strong revenue growth we delivered this quarter, orders continue to significantly exceed revenue, strengthening our visibility into future activity and supporting our confidence in the continued growth of this business.

Orders during the quarter included both initial awards and follow-on commitments that move programs from development into low rate production. International demand continues to support our growth. While international customers have historically represented about 15% of revenue, their share of our backlog has grown substantially in the fiscal year, accounting now for nearly 1/4 of our total backlog. Tim Paulin: Thank you, Brian. We're now on Slide 6. Our third quarter results reflect both growth in customer demand and faster pace of activity on existing programs. I'll walk through the financial detail on Slide 6, and then we'll cover free cash flow and our balance sheet. As Brian mentioned, revenue was $194 million, up 90% year-over-year or 89% organically, reflecting increased activity in Air & Missile Defense, integrated satellite payload programs and allied maritime programs. Adjusted EBITDA increased 91% to $28.5 million with a margin of 14.7%.

Higher revenue and cost actions offset the program mix, including more upfront engineering and initial production on programs where we are embedding our proprietary technology as well as growing investment in public company capabilities. As these programs move into higher rate production, we expect to benefit from the engineering work already completed and greater manufacturing scale. On a GAAP basis, we reported a net loss of $5 million or $0.04 per share compared to a net loss of $3.5 million or $0.03 per share in the prior year period. Adjusted net income was $17 million or $0.15 per share versus $1.7 million and $0.02 per share in the prior period.

Our adjusted net income measure excludes acquisitions and integration-related costs, stock-based compensation, amortization of acquired intangibles and certain other items together with related tax effects. The year-over-year improvement in adjusted net income was primarily driven by stronger results of operations, lower interest expense and adjustments for onetime items such as share-based compensation and loss on debt extinguishment. Turning to our results for the 9 months ended September 30, 2026. Revenue increased 55% to $435 million, reflecting stronger growth on new and existing programs. On a GAAP basis, we reported a net loss of $18 million or $0.17 per share compared to a net loss of $13.2 million or $0.14 per share in the prior year period.

Adjusted net income was $30.6 million or $0.28 per share versus $2.4 million and $0.03 per share in the prior period. The increase in our net loss is mainly attributable to nonrecurring stock-based compensation expenses and a loss on refinancing debt, partially offset by stronger operational performance and lower interest expense. Adjusted EBITDA grew 65% to $66.3 million, supported by top line growth and effective cost controls, yielding an adjusted EBITDA margin of 15.2%, a year-over-year increase of 90 basis points. Reconciliations of adjusted EBITDA, adjusted net income, adjusted diluted earnings per share and free cash flow to the corresponding GAAP measures are included in our earnings materials. Turning now to free cash flow.

Operating activities generated approximately $84 million of cash in the quarter, while capital expenditures were $5 million, resulting in a free cash flow of $79 million. Free cash flow excludes IPO proceeds. Through the first 9 months, operating cash flow was $119 million, capital expenditures were $11 million, core free cash flow of $108 million. Lyntris delivered strong free cash flow this quarter, supported by earnings and favorable customer payments. Across our portfolio, we received payments at different points in program execution, including upfront funding, progress payments and payments following delivery. We work with customers to align payment terms with program requirements and reduce the working capital required for growth.

Our mix of payment structures, disciplined working capital management, and low capital intensity support an attractive cash flow profile. Cash flow will vary from quarter-to-quarter as receipts and program spending move through the business. We expect continued strong cash generation as we execute our backlog, further strengthening our balance sheet and financial flexibility. We also took important steps to strengthen our balance sheet during the quarter. In July, we entered into a new $200 million term loan plus $100 million revolving credit facility, which came with materially lower interest rates than our prior facilities. Additionally, we used about $60 million of IPO proceeds to repay debt and ended the quarter with no balance on our revolver.

We ended the quarter with $88 million in cash and $198 million in debt, bringing net leverage to 1.2x, down significantly from 4.2x at the beginning of the fiscal year. Looking ahead, we expect net leverage to continue declining over time, although working capital requirements may lead to some quarter-over-quarter variability. Our strengthened balance sheet provides greater financial flexibility to support customer commitments, fund working capital needs, and invest in future growth. With that, I'll turn it over to Matt to discuss our capabilities and progress we're making across key programs. Matt?

Matthew Alty: Thank you, Tim. Let's now turn to Slide 7. I'd like to start by taking a step back and examining the mission environment because it explains why customers choose Lyntris. Warfare has changed in three fundamental ways. Firstly, our adversaries are adapting faster and the threats we encounter are more complex and numerous across every domain. We operate in a spectrum that is now congested, contested and weaponized. And detecting, tracking and responding to these threats require sensors with more range, sensitivity, and accuracy. Second, the data. Following the proliferation of sensor networks, data often remains siloed by service and platform, which is a problem when decision time lines are compressed.

Commanders need a clear integrated view of the battle space that enables faster, more informed decisions. Third, connectivity. Adversaries of industrialized electronic warfare and legacy architectures, satellites and waveforms can become single points of failure. The United States and its allies need secure, resilient links. And many allied nations are building sovereign capabilities to protect their own borders. Together, these dynamics are reshaping mission requirements and creating significant opportunities for Lyntris. Turning to Slide 8. Lyntris' capabilities cover the full path from sensing to action. Our sensors are used to detect threats and communicate data in highly contested environments. Our sensor architecture shapes how those sensors behave and prepares their output to be fused with other sources.

Our data and mission software then turns that information into an integrated picture that supports faster, more informed decisions. Our solutions are modular by design. We build proven hardware and software building blocks that can be adapted for different platforms and missions so a customer can start with a single component and scale to a fully integrated subsystem. That modularity is why our technology appears in every domain from integrated satellite payloads and into subsystems to radar on next-generation fighters, multiband ground terminals and maritime systems. The platforms differ, but the same core technology carries across each one.

Together, these capabilities support the 3 missions that Brian described earlier, Maritime Domain Awareness, Air & Missile Defense, and Space ISR & Resilient Communications. Slide 9 shows how we bring those capabilities to market. Our merchant vendor supplier model gives us multiple paths to participate in customer programs. We work with both established defense primes and newer entrants and our technologies often support more than one team competing for the same opportunity. We also work directly with end users, including the U.S. services and allied governments. Engaging early helps us understand their requirements and build our proprietary technology into the solutions that can advance with the program. Proprietary technology is central to that approach.

Approximately 85% of our product revenue comes from products built on design IP that we own. And the vast majority of our business comes from sole, single or directed source positions. As of the end of last year, we supported more than 200 programs. Those IP-derived positions provide continuity as programs advance and they are the foundation for the program momentum on the next slide. Let's turn to Slide 10, where 3 programs show how our capabilities address the needs we described earlier and how our role can grow over time. We'll begin with Air & Missile Defense.

LTAMDS is a program that we've supported from concept, and the program has recently transitioned into production and deployment phase under a U.S. Army contract valued at over $1.7 billion to the prime. In September, we announced production orders under a long-term purchase agreement with Raytheon, supporting demand through 2028. LTAMDS has been developed to provide the Army with 360-degree integrated Air & Missile Defense capabilities. The precision thermal management assemblies that we build at Lyntris help the radar's high-power electronics maintain stable temperatures and directly support the radar sensitivity, accuracy and range. Detecting and tracking the threat, however, is only the first step.

In Maritime Domain Awareness, our customers need to interpret data faster so they can make informed decisions, develop a plan and coordinate a response. Our command-and-control solutions bring information from multiple sensors into a shared operational picture, enabling faster, more informed decisions. For the Navy's Maritime Tactical Command and Control Program, or MTC2, we deliver a command and control platform that combines data integration, visualization and mission planning. It helps fleet planners at sea and at shore to understand the operating environment, plan missions, and coordinate operations. In Morocco, we adapted our Garda C2 technology to connect distributed sensors, operational sensors, mobile systems and ships, creating a common operating picture tailored to the Morocco Navy's requirements.

In Egypt, we are applying that approach to an awarded Maritime Domain Awareness program that brings together coastal sensors, operational centers, and command and control software. Each is an example of an established technology reaching another customer through an architecture tailored to its needs. In Space ISR & Resilient Communications, we're taking on a broader payload role. Earlier this month, we announced our selection as the prime payload integrator supporting the U.S. Space Force's Protected Tactical Satellite Communications Global Program or PTS-G. Our work spans radio frequency architecture, pointing systems, antenna and full payload integration and testing at our antenna center of excellence in Longmont, Colorado.

Building on 20 years of space heritage, this program expands our role from integrated antenna solutions to integrated satellite payloads. The same RF and antenna capabilities apply to sovereign payload opportunities that Brian described earlier. Many international customers need increasingly complex satellite systems that can operate in contested environments, often on compressed schedules. Building on established technology allows us to reduce technical risk and quickly adapt designs to their specific mission requirements. Together, these programs show how we leverage established technology, expand our role in mission-critical programs and create additional paths for growth. Slide 11 shows how those positions can develop through 4 stages: develop, deploy, expand, and sustain & upgrade.

The stages can overlap and we participate at different points across programs. In develop, we help establish the architecture and solve technical challenges on well-funded, high-priority customer programs. This upfront engineering work embeds our proprietary technology in the customer system and positions us for repeat production, incremental content, and margin expansion as the program scales. In deploy, we integrate and field the solution drawing on established designs, manufacturing processes and software. The LTAMDS program I shared a moment ago is a prime example where we are scaling production of thermal management technology to directly support a high-growth program. In expand, we bring that technology to additional customers or missions or take on more of an existing system.

Expansion can also mean leveraging the same proprietary technology to address a similar requirement on an adjacent program. For example, our thermal management IP supports multiple AE or radar programs and our RF and precision pointing technologies support multiple SATCOM programs, both domestically and internationally. Because we're a merchant supplier, we can support multiple customer teams at the same time. So an investment in our IP extends well beyond any single program award. Leveraging established technology and increasing production volumes can improve program economics over time.

In sustain & upgrade, we support fielded systems and add capabilities as requirements change or the system is upgraded to adapt to an emerging threat or emission requirement, including internationally, as we are doing with the Captor-E Mk2 radar upgrade for the U.K. Typhoon fleet. We support customers with programs at different stages of this life cycle. Programs entering production today often reflect years of earlier engineering work. At the same time, the development work we undertake today helps establish positions that can support growth for many years to come. Participating early allows us to help customers solve demanding technical requirements and incorporate our proprietary technology into the solution.

Successful execution then gives us a foundation to support subsequent deployments, production orders and upgrades. The mix of activity across these stages may affect margins from period to period. Our objective is to improve the profitability of established programs while building the next generation of growth opportunities. Back to Brian.

Brian Morrison: Thanks, Matt. That life cycle progression that Matt talked about is fundamental to our long-term growth strategy. We see opportunities to expand our role on existing programs, broaden the solutions we provide, and bring our technology to new customers and missions. Our priority is to translate those opportunities into sustained growth and strong financial performance. We're focused on aligning engineering, suppliers and production capacity with the commitments we already have in hand. We're also bringing more capabilities together around customer requirements. Our task now then is to turn product improvements into consistent execution and measurable financial results. Turning to Slide 12. I'll start with our fiscal 2026 outlook.

For full year 2026, we expect revenue of $623 million to $630 million, representing approximately 61% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. Adjusted EBITDA of $95.5 million to $97 million or expected growth of about 54%. We expect growth to come from increased activity on established Air & Missile Defense programs, continued integrated payload execution and delivery against already awarded maritime programs. Backlog conversion and follow-on orders support that opportunity with customer schedules and award timing influencing the pace of revenue. Our margin assumptions reflect higher volume, improved operating efficiency and a greater contribution from our technology, partly offset by continued initial fielding activity and investment to support growth.

With more design and initial deployment work than we had initially anticipated, we now expect adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to occur over a somewhat longer period than initially anticipated, although that work is helping us to overdrive EBITDA and revenue today. We remain confident in our long-term margin improvement strategy. Our work embeds our IP and customer solutions and creates opportunities for higher margin repeat production as programs expand. And as I suggested, we welcome the additional revenue and adjusted EBITDA dollars associated with this increased volume. We're building Lyntris around differentiated technologies, strong positions on critical programs and the ability to deliver integrated solutions across connected missions.

Our priorities are clear: execute consistently, expand our proprietary content, and drive greater efficiency as we scale. By doing so, we believe we can strengthen our competitive position, capture a greater share of our customers' evolving needs, and translate that growth into higher earnings and stronger cash generation over time. I want to thank our employees for their expertise and commitment, which helped us drive these results. I want to thank our customers for their trust and our shareholders for joining us on this next chapter. We look forward to updating you on our progress. With that, I'll take your questions.

#3228. You Should Update to iOS 27.2 Now to Patch Hundreds of Bugs

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems

The update fixes some bugs that could expose your sensitive iPhone data or worse.

Apple released iOS 27.2 on Monday, Oct. 26, just a few days after the launch of the iPhone Duo. While iOS 27.2 brings Siri AI to more languages and updates a few other features, it also patches 141 bugs and security issues, including some that could allow a third party to access data or run commands on your iPhone or leave your device inoperable.

You can download iOS 27.2 now by going to Settings > General > Software Update > Update Now and following the prompts on your screen.

According to Apple’s release notes, iOS 27.2 patches dozens of issues across your iPhone. Some of these issues can cause some serious problems for you and your device.

Nine of these bugs address issues that could lead to kernel corruption on your device. The kernel is the core of your device’s operating system, and kernel corruption can cause your device to freeze or crash. The blue screen of death, for example, could be caused by kernel corruption.

Apple also wrote that seven of these bugs could lead to arbitrary code execution. That means the bug could allow a third party to steal your data or use your device for other nefarious purposes.

The update addresses a lot of other bugs, including one that you might run into if you plug a malicious USB into your device. Apple didn’t write that any of these bugs were being actively exploited, but you should still update to iOS 27.2 now to give yourself the most protection.

For as many bugs as 27.2 fixes, it’s actually a slight decrease from earlier updates. Last month’s iOS 27 update patched even more bugs at 157. The number of bug fixes in both iOS updates are unusual based on data over the past few years. In iOS 26, the most bug fixes included in an update was 88 with iOS 26.6. The update with the next highest number of patches was iOS 18.4 with 75.

Apple didn’t say why there’s been an uptick in the number of bug fixes in iOS updates. Artificial intelligence has been used recently to find and address huge numbers of software bugs; however, that doesn’t appear to be the cause behind the surge in iOS 27.2 or iOS 27. Apple usually notes when a bug is found with the help of AI, yet OpenAI is mentioned four times in iOS 27.2’s release notes, and Claude’s Anthropic is only mentioned thrice.

Apple didn’t immediately respond to my request to comment.

For more iOS news, here’s what you should know about iOS 27.2 and iOS 27.1. You can also check out our iOS 27 cheat sheet.

#3227. Apple TV renews ‘Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars’ for season three

Award-winning culinary show ‘Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars’ is getting a third season, in an announcement that came hours after its second season came to a close. Here are the details.

Just as ‘Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook’ premiered with a two-episode combo, and ‘Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars’ aired its second season finale, the company confirmed that the latter will return for an eight-episode third season.

‘Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars’ is hosted by Topjaw’s Jesse Burgess and executive produced by Gordon Ramsay. Each season tells the story of several restaurants around the world as they compete to earn, retain, or increase their Michelin Star ratings.

#3222. 3 ways Bluetooth 7 upgrades your devices beyond lossless audio

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Bluetooth Core 7.0 could make your smart home devices easier to set up, for one. Here's what we know about the new core specification.

Bluetooth Core 7.0 is here, and each new specification from the Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG) offers a glimpse of what we can expect from our devices in the future. The major feature incorporated into the new core standard is High Data Throughput (HDT), which can enable lossless wireless audio and improved multi-channel spatial audio on more Bluetooth devices.

Also: Apple has a Bluetooth problem, and Android is taking advantage

Bluetooth Core 7.0’s standout feature is that it can achieve wireless lossless audio. However, the improvements to the Bluetooth stack architecture — particularly, expanding the Bluetooth spectrum — allow for faster data transfer, improved energy efficiency, more resilient connections, and create more room for devices and their data-intensive applications.

HDT means good news for audiophiles, smart home enthusiasts, VR/XR fans, wellness wearable aficionados, AI companion devotees, and much more. I explained applications of HDT in a wireless audio context earlier this year. Now that it’s officially adopted, here’s what you can expect.

A major milestone in Bluetooth Core 7.0 is the ability to stream lossless audio over a wireless connection. Bluetooth is lossy, requiring data compression that diminishes audio quality. HDT’s faster data transfer and greater wireless data capacity enable it to handle the massive volume of data required to achieve lossless quality.

Also: Your Bose headphones are getting a major Bluetooth upgrade – what to expect

Audiophiles typically avoid wireless headphones for intensive listening due to the necessary data compression, opting for wired headphones that can accommodate larger lossless files. Bluetooth’s innovation here is widely regarded as a major leap in wireless technology.

HDT also promises to standardize spatial audio, with expanded data transfers allowing for multi-channel audio setups. Standardizing this form of audio transmission could mean consumers can expect more affordable brands and products to adopt this premium feature.

Every consumer-friendly feature possible within Bluetooth Core 7.0 can be traced back to its ability to accommodate more devices and their ever-expanding data needs. According to a Bluetooth blog post, Bluetooth HDT delivers nearly four times the previous maximum Bluetooth throughput.

Data throughput is the amount of data received, transmitted, and processed over the Bluetooth network. With nearly four times the processing power, HDT can move more data, faster. HDT increases Bluetooth’s maximum supported bitrate to 7.5 Mbps, up from the current 2 Mbps.

Also: Beware of Bluetooth sniffers: How your favorite gadgets could be exposing your data

The result is shorter download times for a device’s firmware update, faster device location when Find My Device is activated, or faster transfer of a large photo album via Android’s QuickShare or Apple’s AirDrop.

In the same blog post, Øyvind Strøm, executive vice president of the short-range business unit at Nordic Semiconductor, gives examples of a smartwatch syncing hours’ worth of workout data to your phone in seconds, or a pair of headphones, a smart speaker, or a security camera that can download a firmware update with nearly zero interruption to the user experience.

In a smart home context, Bluetooth Low Energy (LE) is the wireless technology that works in the background, connecting your devices. Bluetooth LE is the baseline technology for quick device discovery and connection. The most recent example of this is Apple’s HomeView, which uses Bluetooth LE to discover a nearby, trusted iPhone to unlock that user’s personalized home hub display.

The less you feel its presence through lags, wait times, and dropouts, the better it’s working. HDT’s goal is to make Bluetooth connectivity frictionless, which is especially valuable when your smart lights, shades, speakers, TVs, refrigerators, and more rely on the technology.

Also: Forget Wi-Fi: Apple is betting on Bluetooth with its new home devices

For example, HDT’s improved data throughput could allow doorbells, cameras, and robot vacuums to quickly offload large amounts of data to your smart home hub. It could also enable near-instantaneous setup of a new device onto your smart home network and firmware updates.

Finally, HDT also addressed network stability and reliability, especially in high-traffic areas such as apartment complexes and dense cities, where a busy network can cause delays and backups. Alongside improvements to Wi-Fi and Thread, a truly seamless smart home is on the horizon.

Bluetooth’s Human Interface Device (HID) profile refers to the wireless communication used by peripheral devices, such as mice, keyboards, and game controllers, when connecting to a host device. Smart glasses and controllers connected to XR/VR headsets also use this profile, and their data-intensive computing will benefit greatly from HDT.

Devices using the HID profile can expect HDT to lay the foundation for making cloud gaming more reliable, spatial computing more responsive, and offloading audio/visual data from smart glasses less power-intensive.

Also: Frustrated with your Bluetooth? How multipoint works – and why it sometimes won’t

Additionally, gaming keyboards and mice can expect HDT’s expanded data processing to deliver shorter device communication intervals, reducing latency and lag.

In 2026, we’re starting to see more Bluetooth Core 6.0-equipped devices, with Samsung’s recently announced Galaxy Buds On featuring Bluetooth 6.2. Though Bluetooth’s blog post states that the first application of HDT will be for premium wireless audio, many audio manufacturers are behind, still releasing products with Bluetooth 5.4.

Smartphones, smartwatches, and smart home products tend to move a little faster, with the majority of current Bluetooth Core 6.0 products falling into these categories.

The Bluetooth SIG announced Auracast in 2022, and audio manufacturers are now beginning to adopt this technology more widely. Channel Sounding was released with Bluetooth Core 6.0 in 2024, with some early adopters releasing compatible products this year, including Google’s Pixel Tag and Motorola’s Moto Tag 2; more are expected next year and into 2028. With these adoption cycles in mind, we may be well into the next decade before HDT becomes standard.

#3221. The Step-by-Step Guide to Shutting Off Apple Intelligence Features in iOS 27

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

With the master Apple Intelligence toggle gone, opting out in iOS 27 means turning off Siri AI, Writing Tools, Image Playground and other features separately.

Screen Time, the iPhone feature most people know for limiting app use, has become the most direct way to block Apple Intelligence in iOS 27. That’s because Apple removed the single switch that used to turn every AI feature off at once. The Settings section once called Apple Intelligence & Siri is now just Siri, centered on the new Siri AI, and the remaining AI tools are scattered across several menus. Screen Time’s restrictions can shut down Writing Tools and image creation together, and a few other features need their own toggles. Here’s the full map.

Individual features can still be disabled, but they’re scattered across several menus in Settings and Screen Time rather than consolidated in one place. Here’s the current map of what can be turned off and where to find each control.

If your device is not running the newest software, turning off Apple Intelligence all at once only takes a few taps in Settings and doesn’t affect any core iPhone functionality. Here’s how to do it on iPhone, iPad and Mac.

You can still disable some of Apple’s AI features if your iPhone is running iOS 27. It just won’t be as easy as tapping the main toggle.

To disable Siri AI, go to Settings > Siri and toggle off the control. Beware, though, that this will disable your voice assistant entirely, as well as disable conversations in the new dedicated Siri app and block you from using Apple’s Visual Intelligence. Additionally, your HomePod speakers will not be able to recognize your voice or help with personal content if they’re on the same iCloud account as your iPhone.

Keep reading for how to disable some of the individual Apple AI features.

Since the first Apple Intelligence features rolled out in iOS 18.1, some people have opted out of the new technology. Tools such as Image Playground, Genmoji and message summaries can use up to 7GB of your device’s internal storage — a sizable chunk, especially if you tend to run against the upper limit of its free space.

Even if storage is not an issue, you just may not be interested in Apple’s set of AI features. A recent CNET survey finds that just 19% of US smartphone owners are choosing to upgrade their devices to take advantage of new AI features. And a recent ZDNET/Aberdeen survey reveals that the majority of US adults say they will not use most AI features, and just 8% would consider paying extra for them. Some AI features are more welcome than others, with 58% of respondents saying using AI for photo editing would be valuable.

Or, honestly, you may not want to deal with features that are creating inaccurate summaries or that can be replicated without Apple Intelligence.

(Earlier iOS 18 updates re-enabled Apple Intelligence automatically even if you had turned it off, but as of iOS 18.4, the setting is honored.)

Read more: Did a well-meaning friend send you a message about Apple Intelligence possibly reading your private information? Here’s what’s actually going on.

I’m not an AI crank — I appreciate features such as notification summaries and the Clean Up tool in the Photos app. And yet, Apple Intelligence is also a work in progress, an evolving set of features that Apple is heavily hyping while gradually developing. I wouldn’t hold it against you if you wanted to not be distracted or feel like you’re doing Apple’s testing for them (that’s what the developer and public betas should be for).

Remember that Apple Intelligence works only on the new iPhone 18 lineup, the iPhone Duo, iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, iPhone 17E, iPhone 16, iPhone 16E, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro or M-series Macs and iPads, plus the newest iPad mini.

If you’re concerned about the storage requirements of Apple Intelligence, you can find out how much the system is using by going to Settings > General > iPhone (or iPad) Storage > iOS (or iPadOS).

See how much space Apple Intelligence is using in Settings. This is what it looks like running iOS 26, but the settings flow is the same.

Note that even after turning off Apple Intelligence, the storage still shows up in the iOS Storage list. However, I was able to confirm that if the phone’s storage fills up and the system needs that now-inactive space, iOS reclaims what it needs.

Maybe you’re finding some Apple Intelligence features helpful while others are annoying (or just highly amusing). You can turn off specific features in the settings for apps to which they apply.

For example, to disable text summaries in Messages notifications, go to Settings > Apps > Messages and switch off the Summarize Messages option.

Some features are not as app-specific. Writing Tools, which use Apple Intelligence to proof or rewrite text, appear as an option when you select text, regardless of the app. To turn that off, you need to disable Apple Intelligence system-wide.

Also note that nearly every app includes an “Apple Intelligence & Siri” option in Settings, with a Learn from this App option (turned on by default). That applies just to whether Apple Intelligence and Siri can monitor how you use it to make suggestions; it doesn’t affect any particular Apple Intelligence features.

Another option for restricting what Apple Intelligence can do is buried in the Screen Time settings. Screen Time is designed to control which apps and features can run on another device, such as the iPhone used by a child in your household. But it’s also helpful for tracking how much time you’re spending on the device and, in this case, turning off some components of Apple Intelligence.

Turn off selected Apple Intelligence features in the Screen Time settings. This is what the settings look like with iOS 26. It may look different if you are using iOS 27. The settings flow is the same.

If you haven’t upgraded to iOS 27 yet, make a good backup first.

If you aren’t on iOS 27, you can turn off Apple Intelligence with one tap. (You can see what software your iPhone is running by going to Settings > General > About and seeing what iOS version you’re running.)

If you’re on iOS 26 or earlier, here’s how to disable Apple Intelligence. Open Settings (iPhone or iPad) or System Settings (Mac) and choose Apple Intelligence & Siri. Then turn off the Apple Intelligence option. Confirm your choice in the dialog that appears by tapping Turn Off Apple Intelligence.

Turn off Apple Intelligence entirely with one switch if you are running iOS 26 or an earlier software version.

Curiously, the Clean Up tool in Photos sticks around even when Apple Intelligence is turned off, perhaps because the first time you use it the app downloads resources for it and holds onto them.
