#3050. Seahawks release RB Velus Jones Jr., clear spot on active roster

Although the Seattle Seahawks remain in the midst of an injury crisis ahead of their crucial Week 9 clash against their division rival Arizona Cardinals, they'll have some some room to work with after Friday's roster shuffle.

The team announced they released running back Velus Jones Jr. and subsequently re-signed him to their practice squad, where they had a vacant spot. As a vested veteran, he was not subject to waivers.

With Jones Jr. reverting to the practice squad, Seattle now has an open spot on their 53-man roster.

Through three games, Jones Jr. logged 28 yards on nine carries, but suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 7 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs and was forced to miss Monday's game against the Chicago Bears.

Although he practiced in a limited capacity on both Wednesday and Thursday, the return of running backs Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet on top of the team already committed to Emanuel Wilson as well as George Holani likely would've made him odd man out even if he was deemed healthy enough to return.

With DT Leonard Williams (stinger), OG Quenton Nelson (knee), WR Rashid Shaheed (knee), LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), QB Sam Darnold (quadriceps, ribs), Brandon Pili (back), and OT Charles Cross (ankle) already ruled out, the Seahawks appear poised to fill the vacant spot with a player of one of those seven positions and they'll have plenty of options to choose from.

While WR Montorie Foster Jr. was elevated against the Bears, Seattle signed QB Adrian Martinez and linebacker Jamie Sheriff to their practice squad on Wednesday, seemingly hinting one of them could take the final spot.

Alongside Nwosu's injury, LB Connor O'Toole (foot) is deemed questionable and if he's ultimately ruled out, Sheriff fits the bill especially given his experience with the team. However, the Seahawks are currently poised to have just two quarterbacks (Drew Lock, Jalen Milroe) on the roster for Sunday's game, so it wouldn't be surprising if the opted to add a third, considering Milroe's inexperience.

The Seahawks are set to announce their game elevations on Saturday afternoon.

#3045. Malik Nabers makes his status clear after Giants injury scare: ‘I practiced!’

Malik Nabers ran off the field and yelled "I practiced!" almost loud enough for fans in Philadelphia to hear.

After his absence from Thursday's practice because of knee discomfort caused some unrest among Giants fans, Nabers was back Friday and didn't want anyone to have to wait two extra hours until the release of the injury report to know that he is ready to face the Eagles on Sunday.

"It's not an issue," head coach John Harbaugh said. "He'll be full-go for the game."

How significant is that? Forget Nabers' four straight 100-yard games and consider what quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan told J.J. McCarthy when he made his season debut.

Malik Nabers #1 of the New York Giants warms up during a game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026, in Houston. Getty Images

"He was kind of getting his feet wet, a little shaky to start," Callahan said. "He came back to the sideline and I said, 'Hey dude, No. 1 (Nabers) and No. 9 (Isaiah Likely), as much as you can possibly find them.' That's how good offenses work. He's learning."

The Giants had been linked to DTs Jeffery Simmons and Da'Ron Payne on the trade market. Neither is coming, but another defensive tackle might.

"The more, the merrier," D.J. Reader told The Post. "Another guy comes in, hopefully he can help us. I respect all the guys around the league. And I think somebody would want to be a part of us. We have a good thing going."

Reader (57.1 percent) and Shelby Harris (53.9 percent) have played most of the snaps. With Chauncey Golston sidelined, Darius Alexander, C.J. Okoye and Bobby Jamison-Travis are trying to find footing.

New York Giants defensive tackle DJ Reader (98) looks on during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium in Houston, Oct. 25, 2026. Getty Images

"You have to trust that the people upstairs and Harbaugh are going to make the best decisions," Harris said. "You can't dwell on those decisions. We're just trying to win. It doesn't matter if I play 50 snaps, 20 snaps or five snaps."

If catching a punt isn't hard enough already, try doing it with one healthy hand.

Charlie Jones (questionable) tried that Thursday but was back to two hands and wearing a brace Friday.

Jones underwent surgery on a broken thumb as a rookie in 2023.

New York Giants wide receiver Charlie Jones (89) catches a kickoff against the New Orleans Saints in East Rutherford, N.J., Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

"I'm comfortable," Jones said. "Just going to see if they're comfortable with me. With things like this, it's nice to get out there and tell your brain, 'You can do it.' Today went well."

Safety Jevon Holland is next in line if Jones can't go. Leaving a starter susceptible to big hits as a returner is "not ideal," Harbaugh said.

"If we have to do it, we will," he added. "Jevon's really good. I don't have any worries, any qualms about Jevon at all. Knowing him, he'd be thrilled."

The Giants have an open spot on the 53-man roster and "there's a reason for it." Harbaugh indicated it was for an internal promotion.

QB Jaxson Dart was maneuvering through the locker room on crutches and joking with teammates during the media window for the first time since his Sept. 21 injury.

RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) will play for the Eagles but WR Devonta Smith (hamstring) will not.

The Federal Reserve Board on Friday released the results of the 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances, which provides the public and policymakers with detailed insights into the economic condition of American families.

The data provide a representative picture of what Americans own, how and how much they borrow, and how they bank. The current version of the survey has been undertaken every three years since 1989 and provides the public with an extensive time series of thorough information on the economic conditions of American families. Alongside the survey data, the Board issued its summary report entitled Changes in U.S. Family Finances from 2022 to 2025 (PDF), which examines changes in income, net worth, assets, debt, and financial vulnerability.

In addition to the summary report, an interactive chartbook displaying changes in these financial characteristics over time is available here. Additional data from the survey, including extensive data examining other economic conditions of American families, is made available to researchers and the public here.

The survey is conducted for the Board by NORC, a social science research organization at the University of Chicago. Participants in the study are chosen at random from 119 geographic areas, including metropolitan areas and rural counties across the United States, using scientific sampling procedures that aim to produce a sample representative of American families.

#3042. Prediction market traders say an Anthropic IPO is near-certain this year after company filed with SEC

Anthropic on Monday unveiled its Form S-1 filing, taking the company one step closer to completing its long-awaited move to the public markets, which is now seen as almost guaranteed to come this year.

Speculators on prediction market platform Kalshi place 95% odds that the artificial intelligence giant officially announces an initial public offering by the end of 2026.

Kalshi defines officially announcing an IPO as either the Securities and Exchange Commission declaring an S-1 effective, a priced IPO or an exchange assigning a ticker to a stock.

The Anthropic S-1 envisions a Nasdaq Stock Market ticker symbol of "ANT."

Anthropic is aiming to start trading the week of Nov. 16, according to a report in the Wall Street Journal. Traders on Kalshi place just a 14% chance that the company begins trading before then.

On the Polymarket platform, traders give a 69% chance that Anthropic will list on a public exchange and open for trading by Nov. 20.
